title: Add scratch-only Python rename stage
summary: Enable one Python-backed, scratch-only single-file rename stage with strict mutation evidence while leaving production naming and media processing in PowerShell.
reason: Rename is the lowest-risk disabled stage because Python already owns transactional rename primitives and this slice can be confined to temporary scratch data without FFmpeg, subtitle, audio, publish, drain, source, output, or final-library mutation.
behavior_before: The dispatcher enabled read-only probe/decide and guarded PowerShell ingest; rename was a descriptive disabled contract.
behavior_after: The dispatcher additionally enables Python rename for exactly one regular file already inside a dispatcher-allowed scratch root disjoint from dispatcher-protected source roots; payload roots must match the trusted runner configuration. Dry-run returns a content-bound fingerprint. Execute requires confirm_apply=true, UUID operation identity, matching fingerprint, command and operation journals, no overwrite or extension change, content-hash equality, and a scratch-local undo record. PowerShell entrypoint rename remains disabled and the production pipeline remains unchanged.
tests_added: tests.python.desktop.test_stage_entrypoint: PowerShell dispatcher compatibility keeps rename disabled
tests.python.desktop.test_stage_runner: scratch rename confirmation, path/source boundaries, fingerprint, journals, duplicate replay, undo evidence, and rollback

rollback_plan: Set rename execution_backend back to disabled, remove run_rename_stage and src/mediapipeline/core/rename/stage.py, restore the descriptive RenamePayload/Result contract, regenerate the stage schema and pipeline map, and rerun the focused stage/rename/path-boundary validation. notes:
Python impact: additive dispatcher executor and stricter rename DTO only. No Local API route, WebView control, PowerShell production entrypoint, FFmpeg policy, source mutation, output placement, pending publish, or final-library behavior is added. Real-media validation is not required for this scratch-name-only fixture slice; any future production naming cutover remains separately gated.
